system.name: Apparate
system.one_liner: a system that automatically applies and manages early exits in ML models to ease the throughput-latency tension in inference serving

content.subject: how a batch of 16 samples shrinks as some exit early at each layer's ramp instead of continuing

content.key_idea: Augmenting each layer of a DNN with a lightweight exit ramp lets easy inputs leave the model as soon as a ramp is confident, so a batch's effective size shrinks layer by layer instead of every input running the full network.
content.reading_order: left to right along the top row of Layers inside the dashed 'Original model' box, dropping down to each Layer's Ramp box and then to its exit-count label, before continuing right to the next Layer with whatever samples remain

evidence: Early exits enable termination of inputs at intermediate layers, lowering both compute and latency.
certain ‘easy’ inputs may not require the full predictive power of a model
results for such inputs may be predictable from the values at intermediate layers

summary: Figure 3 shows the mechanism behind Apparate's early exits (EEs) using one concrete example batch. A batch of 16 samples enters Layer_1 of the dashed-boxed 'Original model'; each layer's output also feeds a green Ramp box that predicts a result and lets confident samples exit immediately rather than run the rest of the network. In this example, 1 sample exits at Ramp_1 (15 continue to Layer_2), 2 more exit at Ramp_2 (13 continue to Layer_3), 2 more exit at Ramp_3 (11 continue), and, after the omitted middle layers, whatever samples remain must exit at the final Ramp_12. Because each ramp only needs to compare its predicted result's entropy against a threshold, the batch's effective size shrinks layer by layer, cutting both compute and latency for the samples that exit early.
